{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01DbGxZxcGytojCNaYudLLLT","type":"tool_result","content":"void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm, parallelized over source rows.\n    // Within iteration k, row k and column k are invariant (the diagonal is\n    // zero and all weights are non-negative), so each source row i != k only\n    // reads row k and writes row i. Rows are therefore independent and the\n    // result is identical to the sequential order. Row k is skipped because\n    // it cannot change, which also keeps rowI and rowK from aliasing.\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    unsigned int* const distData = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* const pathData = path.data();\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n        const unsigned int* const rowK = distData + idx2(0, k, n);\n\n        // Implicit barrier at the end of the loop orders iteration k before k+1\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n            if (i == k) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            unsigned int* const rowI = distData + idx2(0, i, n);\n            unsigned int* const pathI = pathData + idx2(0, i, n);\n            // dist[i][k] is unchanged during this row's update (dist[k][k] == 0)\n            const unsigned int distIK = rowI[k];\n\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n\n                if (newDist < rowI[j]) {\n                    rowI[j] = newDist;\n                    pathI[j] = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n                }\n---\nCMakeLists.txt\nfloydwarshall.cpp","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d505d8ac-bc2d-4311-acf3-0faf95c03382","uuid":"9be7b5af-230d-46f6-a253-03bc98864731","timestamp":"2026-10-12T21:05:09.771Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"void floydWarshall(std::vector<unsigned int>& dist,\n                   std::vector<unsigned int>& path,\n                   const size_t numNodes) {\n    // Classic Floyd-Warshall algorithm, parallelized over source rows.\n    // Within iteration k, row k and column k are invariant (the diagonal is\n    // zero and all weights are non-negative), so each source row i != k only\n    // reads row k and writes row i. Rows are therefore independent and the\n    // result is identical to the sequential order. Row k is skipped because\n    // it cannot change, which also keeps rowI and rowK from aliasing.\n    const size_t n = numNodes;\n    unsigned int* const distData = dist.data();\n    unsigned int* const pathData = path.data();\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n        const unsigned int* const rowK = distData + idx2(0, k, n);\n\n        // Implicit barrier at the end of the loop orders iteration k before k+1\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n            if (i == k) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            unsigned int* const rowI = distData + idx2(0, i, n);\n            unsigned int* const pathI = pathData + idx2(0, i, n);\n            // dist[i][k] is unchanged during this row's update (dist[k][k] == 0)\n            const unsigned int distIK = rowI[k];\n\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n                const unsigned int newDist = distIK + rowK[j];\n\n                if (newDist < rowI[j]) {\n                    rowI[j] = newDist;\n                    pathI[j] = static_cast<unsigned int>(k);\n                }\n---\nCMakeLists.txt\nfloydwarshall.cpp","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01DbGxZxcGytojCNaYudLLLT","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfy2FrLEawndVWTZgXtWh","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Floyd-Warshall benchmark now runs its row updates in parallel with OpenMP. The output is unchanged: the distance-matrix hashes match the original binary for every size and thread count I tried. Only `floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp` and `floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt` changed, the executable name is the same, and no files were added to the repo.\n\n**What changed**\n- **Algorithm:** a single `#pragma omp parallel` region wraps the `k` loop, and each `k` iteration uses `#pragma omp for schedule(static)` over source rows `i`. Within iteration `k`, row `k` cannot change because the diagonal is zero and weights are non-negative. So rows `i != k` are independent, and the parallel result equals the sequential one. Row `k` is skipped, which also prevents aliasing.\n- **Same update order:** the `k`, `i`, `j` loop order and the write-on-improvement logic are preserved, so `path` should match too. `path` is not part of the printed output, so I reasoned about that rather than checking it directly.\n- **CMake:** `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX` on the target. Configuration fails if OpenMP is missing, so there are no `#ifdef` fallbacks.\n- **Left sequential:** matrix initialization and validation. Initialization is untimed and uses `rand_r` in a fixed sequence for reproducibility.\n\n**Verification**\n- Hashes match the original for n ∈ {1, 2, 7, 64, 300, 512, 1000, 2048} at 1, 3, 16 and 256 threads: 32 of 32 configurations.\n- `-v` validation passes at 1, 8 and 256 threads.\n- `-h` and unknown-option handling are unchanged.\n\n**Timing** (minimum of repeated runs on this shared 256-thread EPYC, so treat as approximate)\n\n| n | Original | New, 1 thread | New, best thread count |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 165 ms | ~44 ms | ~9 ms (16 threads) |\n| 2048 | 9382 ms | ~3100 ms | ~70 ms (128 threads) |\n\n**Things to decide**\n- **Thread count:** with no setting, OpenMP uses all 256 logical CPUs. At n=2048 that is slower than 64–128 threads (about 119 ms vs 70 ms), and at n=512 the default-thread run took about 477 ms in one measurement. I did not cap the count in code. Setting `OMP_NUM_THREADS` or hard-capping at the physical core count are both options; tell me which you want.\n- **Race check not clean:** ThreadSanitizer with GCC's libgomp reports races across the per-`k` barrier. I believe this is a false positive from the uninstrumented barrier, since each cross-thread access is separated by one. A clang build with LLVM's libomp hung under TSan, so I could not confirm it cleanly.\n\nScratch builds and binaries are in `/tmp`. I did not commit anything."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1070,"cache_read_input_tokens":42528,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1070},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"d505d8ac-bc2d-4311-acf3-0faf95c03382","uuid":"4a2d6020-4659-4206-9d80-351582cb1c93","timestamp":"2026-10-12T21:05:18.253Z","request_id":"req_011Cfy2FqsC3af7hFVg6DpHA"}
